name: mechanisms
label: Mechanisms of action
description: Controlled mechanism terms. Keep each term to one mechanism, not a mechanism plus its downstream consequence.

terms.label: Non-selective β-adrenergic antagonist
terms.note: Blocks β1 and β2. The β2 blockade is what leaves α-mediated vasoconstriction unopposed when a sympathomimetic is on board.

terms.label: AM404-mediated cannabinoid system modulation
terms.note: Attributed to the metabolite. Record on the AM404 record; the parent record carries the metabolite link.

terms.label: Irreversible COX-1 acetylation
terms.note: Covalent, so the effect outlives the drug and persists for the life of the platelet. This is why aspirin is not interchangeable with a reversible COX inhibitor.

terms.label: Central COX pathway inhibition
terms.note: Reduced CNS prostaglandin synthesis is the consequence, not a separate mechanism.

terms.label: hERG (Kv11.1) potassium channel blockade
terms.note: Off-target. Only reached at supratherapeutic systemic exposure for drugs designed to act in the gut.

terms.label: Peripheral μ-opioid receptor agonist
terms.note: Confined to the myenteric plexus by P-gp efflux at the blood-brain barrier. Saturate or inhibit P-gp and the confinement fails.

terms.label: Covalent protein arylation
terms.note: Electrophilic binding to cysteine residues on cellular protein. The oxidative stress and necrosis that follow are consequences, not separate mechanisms.

terms.label: Gastrointestinal surface-tension reduction (antifoaming)
terms.note: Physical, not receptor-mediated. Nothing is absorbed, which is why this drug is inert in every interaction pair.
